discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of individual spins in solids, establishing solid-state spin-photon interfaces for quantum sensing and quantum networks
motivation: These three physicists showed that a single spin buried in a crystal can be isolated, read out with light and coherently controlled. Wrachtrup pioneered optically detected magnetic resonance of single defect spins, most notably the diamond NV centre. This work founded solid-state quantum sensing, which now reaches nanoscale magnetometry and biosensing. İmamoğlu proposed and demonstrated quantum-dot spin-photon interfaces and cavity quantum electrodynamics with single semiconductor emitters, including spin preparation, strong coupling and spin-photon entanglement. Hanson used these ideas to entangle distant solid-state spins through photons, which led to the first loophole-free Bell test (2015) and multi-node quantum networks. Together they turned individual defects and dots from spectroscopic curiosities into controllable quantum systems. This opened a platform for fundamental tests of quantum mechanics and launched the hardware for quantum sensing and the quantum internet, a field now pursued by hundreds of groups worldwide.
